units.title: Actual Gibbs position moment about a stationary point

sources.label: SPHMC Lemma4.2,(4.6) position moment
sources.scope: Actual normalized volume.tilted(-U),genuine C2 lower/upper Hessian bounds and an explicitly supplied actual stationary point p. The proof establishes normalization,L1,exact position-gradient moment and sharp dimension/curvature bound. General p,positive alpha,finite beta,coordinate-free and zero-dimensional spaces are disclosed extensions. It is not a weakest-hypothesis strong-log-concavity theorem. The source consumer has standardized potential norm(u)^2/2+rho_y(u),p=0,alpha=1,beta=1+eta;stationarity follows from cancellation of the defining linear term. Identification with the affine image of the actual RGO needs the proximal equation and a separate measure-transport proof. No Gaussian transport-Fisher,smoothed-score identity,estimator bias,Picard accuracy,initialization or query-cost theorem is asserted.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space,with its complete metric structure; d=dim_R E may be zero. Volume is its canonical Lebesgue measure.

alpha and beta are nonnegative real numbers,0<alpha and alpha<=beta. U:E->R is twice continuously Frechet differentiable. For every x,v,alpha*norm(v)^2<=D2U(x)[v,v]<=beta*norm(v)^2. The derivatives and gradient are genuine derivatives of U.

p is any supplied point of E satisfying gradient U(p)=0. Existence of a stationary point is not concluded by this theorem. Set Z=integral exp(-U(x)) dx and mu=volume.tilted(-U); the tilt is the actual normalized exponential measure,not an arbitrary probability law.
All displayed real integrals are Bochner integrals. Integrability is proved explicitly; no moment bound or vanishing boundary term is supplied.
units.statement: The actual mu is a probability measure. The function exp(-U) is integrable against volume and its integral Z is strictly positive. Both norm(x-p)^2 and inner(x-p,gradient U(x)) are integrable against mu. Their actual integrals satisfy integral inner(x-p,gradient U(x)) dmu=d and integral norm(x-p)^2 dmu<=d/alpha.
units.boundary: Actual normalized volume.tilted(-U),genuine C2 lower/upper Hessian bounds and an explicitly supplied actual stationary point p. The proof establishes normalization,L1,exact position-gradient moment and sharp dimension/curvature bound. General p,positive alpha,finite beta,coordinate-free and zero-dimensional spaces are disclosed extensions. It is not a weakest-hypothesis strong-log-concavity theorem. The source consumer has standardized potential norm(u)^2/2+rho_y(u),p=0,alpha=1,beta=1+eta;stationarity follows from cancellation of the defining linear term. Identification with the affine image of the actual RGO needs the proximal equation and a separate measure-transport proof. No Gaussian transport-Fisher,smoothed-score identity,estimator bias,Picard accuracy,initialization or query-cost theorem is asserted.

steps.title: Obtain actual Gibbs normalization and gradient integrability
steps.text: Use QuadraticRegularization at zero added precision to derive strong convexity from the genuine Hessian. StrongConvexGibbsIntegrability gives exponential-weight L1. The previously compiled GibbsGradientMoment theorem supplies probability and gradient-square L1 under this same normalized tilt. Its numerical gradient bound is not the final position bound.

steps.title: Derive pointwise coercivity from the actual stationary point
steps.text: Strong convexity gives strong monotonicity of the genuine gradient. Substitute gradient U(p)=0 and use Cauchy-Schwarz. Treat x=p separately before cancelling the positive displacement norm; divide only by alpha>0.

steps.title: Prove position and pairing integrability
steps.text: Dominate position square by gradient square divided by alpha squared. Probability and the bound t<=1+t^2 give position-norm L1. Cauchy-Schwarz and Young give L1 for the position-gradient pairing. These estimates establish integrability only; they do not replace the source sharp constant with beta/alpha squared.

steps.title: Justify every full-space coordinate IBP input
steps.text: For a unit vector v,set f=exp(-U),q(x)=inner(x-p,v),a(x)=D_vU(x). Position and gradient L1/L2 bounds dominate q and qa under the actual tilt. The tilted-integrability equivalence transfers them to volume using the already proved exponential L1. Differentiate the actual functions: D_vq=1 and D_vf=-fa. Thus fq,f D_vq,and (D_vf)q are all integrable before invoking full-space IBP.

steps.title: Evaluate each coordinate and sum the finite basis
steps.text: The justified IBP identity gives integral f*q*a=integral f=Z for every unit basis vector. Sum the finite orthonormal basis and use its inner-product expansion. Every coordinate term is integrable,so finite sums commute with the integral. In dimension zero the sum is empty and yields zero.
steps.formula: \int e^{-U}\langle x-p,v\rangle D_vU\,dx=Z,\qquad\int e^{-U}\langle x-p,\nabla U\rangle\,dx=dZ.

steps.title: Normalize the actual exponential tilt
steps.text: The exponential integral is strictly positive by integral_exp_pos and finite by the established integrability. Apply the actual integral_tilted formula and factor out this same normalizer. Cancelling Z in dZ/Z proves the position-gradient identity under mu.

steps.title: Integrate coercivity to obtain the sharp position moment
steps.text: Both position square and the pairing are integrable. Integrate the pointwise strong-convexity inequality,substitute the exact pairing moment d,and divide by positive alpha. The upper curvature beta was used for the integrability route but does not enter this final constant.

units.lean_statement: Actual Gibbs normalization,L1,position-gradient=d and position-square<=d/alpha with genuine Hessian and stationary-point assumptions.
units.lean_proof: Actual gradient L1 implies position L1;full-space coordinate IBP and finite basis sum;positive normalizer and actual tilt;integrate coercivity.
